__comment: context-guru service dashboard. Provisioned from deploy/grafana/ — see the README there.
Rows answer questions in order: is it up, is it saving money, which components earn their
place, who is using it, is storage healthy, is anything failing.
Series colours are PINNED. Grafana's classic palette cycles hues and repaints the
survivors when a series disappears, so a reader who learned 'blue is actual' gets lied to
after a filter. The three hues (#3987e5 blue, #d95926 orange, #199e70 aqua) validate
colourblind-safe on Grafana's dark surface: worst all-pairs CVD deltaE 9.4, normal-vision
#c98500 and #e66767 are the warning and critical status steps and are used ONLY for status.

ONE RULE for stat and gauge colour: the traffic light (#199e70 / #c98500 / #e66767) means ACT ON THIS — the panel has a threshold an operator should respond to (availability, added latency, filesystem, buffered streams, up/down). Our own magnitudes carry no verdict and are pinned #3987e5 blue: build, request rate, tokens removed, sessions archived, a positive saving, and every bargauge of a raw amount. So green on this dashboard always means a threshold was met that someone might otherwise have had to act on, never merely 'this number is large'.
status, never as a fourth series colour, with the one documented exception of the billed
token tiers where 'output' needs a fourth hue.
Meaning is consistent: BLUE is what happened, ORANGE is the comparison to read it against,
AQUA is a healthy absolute, RED means somebody should act. So the gap is the story.
No panel uses two y-axes. Where two measures have different scales they get two panels —
which is why added latency and upstream latency are not on one chart: 29ms against 19s on
one axis renders the number you care about as a flat line on the floor.
title: context-guru

panels.title: Service
panels.description: 1 when Prometheus last scraped the proxy successfully. DOWN means the process is gone or the port moved — every number below it is then stale, not zero.

panels.title: Build
panels.description: The running version. A value you do not recognise after a deploy means the unit restarted onto the old binary.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Client requests reaching the proxy. A drop to zero while the service is UP is the shape of a broken client credential, not of an idle day.

panels.title: Compaction rate
panels.description: Share of content tokens compaction strips out. Near 0% means the pipeline is running and finding nothing — check the component row below.

panels.title: Added latency
panels.description: Mean time context-guru itself adds per request. This lands on somebody's agent turn, so above ~200ms it is a user-visible cost.

panels.title: Am I saving tokens and money?
Tokens removed this month
panels.description: Deduplicated by content — the honest figure. The gross counter over-counts by roughly 13x because an agent re-sends its whole transcript every turn. Flat while requests climb means compaction stopped acting.

panels.title: Saved this month
panels.description: Baseline spend minus actual spend, across tenants. NEGATIVE is the bad value: compaction is costing more than it saves, usually by churning the provider's prefix cache.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Cache-read tokens over cache-read plus fresh input. Shows n/a at exactly zero: an upstream that reports no cache tiers in its usage block (IBM LiteLLM does not) leaves nothing to divide, and colouring that red would be a false alarm for a condition outside this service's control. Once it reads a real number, a FALL is the first sign compaction is mutating an already-cached prefix and forcing re-writes at ~12x the read price.

panels.title: Expand bounces
panels.description: Times the model had to call context_guru_expand to recover something compaction removed. Any sustained non-zero rate means the pipeline is hiding content the agent still needs, and each bounce costs a whole extra round trip.

panels.title: Spend: actual against baseline
panels.description: Blue is what was billed; orange is what the same traffic would have cost uncompacted. The gap IS the saving — orange meeting or crossing blue means the tool is not paying for itself. One axis on purpose. The third series is what the prompt cache saved over the fresh rate: a separate saving from compaction's, and the one a too-aggressive pipeline spends.

panels.title: Content tokens: before and after compaction
panels.description: Orange is what the agent sent, blue is what reached the provider. The two converging means compaction has stopped removing anything.

panels.title: Billed tokens per minute, by tier
panels.description: What the provider actually charges for. Cache-write climbing while cache-read stays flat is the expensive failure: every write is billed at roughly 12x a read.

panels.title: What compaction itself costs
panels.description: context-guru's own compaction-model spend, kept separate from the agent's bill. Bad is this line approaching the saving on the panel two above — then the tool is spending its winnings.

panels.title: Tokens removed by component
panels.description: The benefit side of each component. A bar at zero is dead weight: it costs latency on every request and removes nothing, so it belongs out of the preset.

panels.title: Hit rate by component
panels.description: How often a component that ran actually changed the request. 0% is the value to act on — it ran on every request and never acted.

panels.title: Time spent in each component
panels.description: The cost side, cumulative since start. A long bar next to a zero bar on the 'tokens removed' panel is a component paying nothing for real latency.

panels.title: Requests per tenant
panels.description: Who is actually using the service. A line pinned flat at a ceiling is a tenant being throttled by TENANT_RPM, not a tenant being quiet.

panels.title: Per-tenant month to date
panels.description: One row per account. A table rather than more coloured series: past a handful of tenants, hues stop being distinguishable. Bad rows are a non-zero 'Disabled', or added latency far above the fleet mean.

panels.title: Is storage and cold storage healthy?
Local database against cold storage
panels.description: Blue is what is still on this box, orange is what moved to Box. Blue climbing while orange stays flat is the bad shape — tiering has stopped and the disk fills.

panels.title: Filesystem in use
panels.description: Crossing 90% starts evicting the oldest sessions. With cold storage ready that is a migration; with it unreachable it is deletion.

panels.title: Cold storage
panels.description: NOT CONFIGURED is the bad value: while it reads that, disk pressure deletes sessions instead of archiving them.

panels.title: Sessions archived
panels.description: Cumulative sessions moved to cold storage. Stuck at zero while the filesystem gauge climbs means eviction is deleting, not tiering.

panels.title: Dropped capture events
panels.description: The capture queue filled and events were discarded. ANY non-zero bar means the dashboard is losing history exactly when load makes it most wanted.

panels.title: Is anything failing?
panels.description: Rate-limit (429) REJECTIONS are not on this row because the proxy exports no counter for them — proxy/limits.go returns the status without recording it. Disabled accounts below are the closest available proxy.

panels.title: Compaction-model failures
panels.description: Timeouts and errors from context-guru's own compaction model. A run of timeouts means the compactor silently did nothing: the arm looks fast because it stopped working.

panels.title: Cache-write churn (frozen decisions flipped)
panels.description: Frozen decisions the store dropped and did not re-derive. Each one flips an already-cached message and forces the provider to re-write the suffix at ~12x the read price. Should sit at zero; anything above it is money.

panels.title: Tokens wasted recovering offloaded content
panels.description: Tokens spent re-serving something compaction removed. This is savings handed back — a rising line means the pipeline is too aggressive for this traffic.

panels.title: Buffered streams
panels.description: Share of responses context-guru had to buffer in full before the client saw a byte. High on traffic that never expands is a straight latency regression.

panels.title: Tenants disabled
panels.description: Accounts the proxy is currently refusing. Anything above zero is somebody's agent failing right now.

panels.title: Expand bounces over time
panels.description: The same recoveries as the stat above, as a trend. A step up right after a config change means the new preset removes something the agent needs.

panels.title: Buffered against streamed responses
panels.description: Orange is responses context-guru had to read in full before the client saw a byte. Orange growing faster than blue is a straight latency regression.

panels.title: Requests refused, by reason
panels.description: Requests turned away before an upstream was called. ANY sustained bar is somebody's agent failing right now. rate_limit and concurrency are both 429 with different fixes (raise TENANT_RPM, raise the in-flight cap), auth/forbidden is a bad or disabled token, no_upstream is our own misconfiguration and upstream_error is the provider.

panels.title: Refusals per tenant
panels.description: Which account is being refused, and for what. This is the panel that tells a quiet tenant apart from a blocked one: a tenant absent from 'Requests per tenant' AND present here is not idle, it is being turned away. Zero everywhere is healthy.

panels.title: Prefix-cache saved this month
panels.description: What context-guru's volatile-tail split saved: counted only where the split ran, the environment snapshot had MOVED since that session's previous request, and the provider then read at least the stable half from cache while writing less than it. The amount is the stable half, not the request's whole cache_read -- a cachesplit-off control arm still read 45,805 tokens, because the agent's other breakpoints match regardless. Priced against a cache MISS (creation rate, 1.25x fresh) because those tokens carry cache_control. EXPECT IT TO BE SMALL on interactive traffic: Claude Code captures its environment block once per session (measured: one distinct tail hash across nine turns and four commits), and a new session finds the previous prefix already expired unless it started inside the provider's 5-minute TTL (measured: 1,105 of 1,127 session starts read zero from cache). The regime where this pays is back-to-back sessions -- which is what the SWE-bench A/B measured at -34.1% cost. The provider's own total cache saving is cg_tenant_cache_saved_usd, a diagnostic.

panels.title: Total avoided this month
panels.description: Our two savings together: compaction (baseline minus actual, minus what our own model calls cost) plus the prefix-cache saving. Two disjoint token sets, both ours, added rather than nested -- the compaction baseline already assumes the cache behaved as it did. It is NOT the cost of an uncached world: the provider's own cache saved far more on the same traffic (cg_tenant_cache_saved_usd) and none of that is credited here.
